newsitem.title: USA: U.N. says all pending Iraq oil contracts approved.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says all pending Iraq oil contracts approved.

text.p: The United Nations said Thursday that it approved another four contracts under the "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq, making a total of five which have passed since the deal formally began earlier this week.
"A total of five contracts have been approved thus far," said U.N. spokesman Sylvana Foa.
Neither Foa nor other U.N. officials would give further details, but other sources have confirmed that two of those contracts are for Turkish state oil concern TUPRAS and Coastal Corp of the U.S.
TUPRAS is expected to contract for 75,000 bpd, while Coastal is expected to lift about 60,000 bpd. Of the other three, one is expected to the resubmitted contract by France's Elf Aquitaine.
Earlier this week, following the official U.N. start to the deal, Iraq's oil minister said that a total of five contracts for $400 million had been approved.

Under the terms of the deal, Iraq can sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months to pay for humanitarian goods for civilians suffering under sanctions for the past six years, as well as other obligations under the Gulf War settlement.
First Iraqi exports are expected to be loaded at the Turkish port of Ceyhan as early as this weekend.
